semantic_correction.stem: A student with type 1 diabetes returns to school after the diabetes care team changes the student’s insulin regimen and continuous glucose monitor settings. Which action by the school nurse is most appropriate?

options.A: Obtain an updated DMMP with the new insulin and CGM instructions, implement it, and ensure trained staff can follow the current routine and emergency plan.
options.B: Continue the prior DMMP until its annual review, while adding verbal notes about the new insulin and CGM settings for the school nurse to use.
options.C: Use written parent instructions to modify the prior DMMP at school and begin the new doses and CGM settings before updated health care orders are received.
options.D: Keep the revised regimen details with the school nurse and let other trained personnel follow the prior DMMP until the diabetes team confirms the changes are working.

semantic_correction.rationale: The American Diabetes Association school-setting statement states that each student with diabetes should have an individualized Diabetes Medical Management Plan (DMMP) developed by the student's health care professional in collaboration with the student and parent or guardian. The DMMP is the basis for school diabetes care and emergency planning and needs to be updated annually or whenever the student's care plan or diabetes management changes. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care also state that school personnel should provide diabetes care in accordance with the individualized DMMP and that students should be supported at school in the use of diabetes technology, including CGM and insulin-delivery devices, as prescribed by the diabetes care team. Therefore A is correct. B delays a needed plan update despite a current regimen change. C asks the school to revise medical orders without the updated health care plan. D creates inconsistent instructions among trained personnel and leaves some staff following an outdated plan.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Coordinate safe school diabetes care by obtaining and implementing an updated individualized DMMP whenever the diabetes regimen or management changes and ensuring relevant trained personnel can follow the current routine and emergency instructions.
semantic_correction.source_document_title: Diabetes Care in the School Setting: A Statement of the American Diabetes Association; 14. Children and Adolescents: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026; 7. Diabetes Technology: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
semantic_correction.source_version_date: ADA school statement published October 25, 2024; Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 published December 8, 2025; current source pages rechecked August 20, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: ADA 2024 school statement, DMMP section: individualized DMMP developed by the student's health care professional with the student and parent/guardian; the DMMP guides school diabetes care and emergency planning and needs to be updated annually or whenever the student's care plan or diabetes management changes. ADA 2026 Section 14, School and Child Care: training of school personnel to provide care in accordance with the individualized DMMP is essential. ADA 2026 Sections 14 and 7: students with diabetes should be supported at school in use of prescribed diabetes technology, including CGM and insulin-delivery systems.
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: School diabetes care should follow an individualized DMMP that is updated when the student's care plan or diabetes management changes, with trained school personnel able to follow current monitoring, treatment, technology, and emergency instructions.
semantic_correction.blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
semantic_correction.blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed p.7 (official PDF pageno 10): identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members; initiate, evaluate and update the client plan of care; assess the need for referrals and obtain necessary orders; advocate for client rights and needs; provide unbiased care and promote equal access to care; recognize limitations and utilize resources.
semantic_correction.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — individualized school diabetes plan, treatment-change communication, and continuity across settings
semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup retained the school-DMMP treatment-change construct, removed the prior only/annual-review cueing, rebuilt A/B/C/D as plausible coordination errors, and shortened the key so it is not uniquely longest.

scope_exclusions.school_policy: The item does not test a district-specific policy, state nursing law, delegation statute, or 504/IEP legal procedure.
scope_exclusions.independent_order_change: The school nurse is not instructed to independently prescribe or rewrite insulin doses or CGM settings; the key requires an updated health care plan/order source.
scope_exclusions.annual_update: Annual review remains appropriate, but a current change in diabetes care is an additional reason to update the DMMP before the next annual review.
scope_exclusions.technology_brand: No CGM, pump, connected pen, or AID brand or device-specific setting is tested.
scope_exclusions.emergency_training: The item tests access to current instructions for relevant trained personnel; it does not specify who may perform each task under every jurisdiction's law.
scope_exclusions.parent_role: Parents/guardians are important collaborators, but parent communication alone does not replace updated medical management instructions when the prescribed regimen changes.

near_duplicate_check.note: Targeted GitHub search for ‘DMMP insulin CGM school updated care plan diabetes management changes’ returned no indexed repository match. No broad bank scan was performed.

option_audit.A: Correct. It obtains the updated individualized plan from the appropriate health care source, implements it, and promotes consistent routine and emergency care among trained school staff.
option_audit.B: Plausible because DMMPs are reviewed annually, but the ADA also requires update when the care plan or diabetes management changes rather than waiting for the annual cycle.
option_audit.C: Plausible because parents communicate important changes, but the school should not substitute parent-written dose/settings changes for an updated health care DMMP/order.
option_audit.D: Plausible because the school nurse often coordinates care, but allowing other trained personnel to use an outdated DMMP creates inconsistent and potentially unsafe care.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. A is the only option that promptly updates the individualized medical plan and keeps school care aligned with current prescribed management. B delays the update, C bypasses the updated health care plan, and D maintains conflicting instructions.

cueing_check.note: The key is tied with C and is not longest; all four are complete school-care coordination actions with comparable clinical detail and no only/all/always/never/every cue.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: NCSBN Management of Care explicitly includes interprofessional collaboration, updating plans of care, referral/order coordination, advocacy, and resource use, directly supporting RN coordination of current diabetes instructions across the school setting.
blueprint_audit.visual_verification: VERIFIED. Official 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan screenshot pageno 10 / printed p.7 was successfully retrieved August 20, 2026 and visibly shows the cited Management of Care activity statements.

source_verification.note: The 2024 ADA school-setting statement and current 2026 Standards Sections 14 and 7 were directly rechecked August 20, 2026. The current school statement explicitly requires DMMP update when the care plan or diabetes management changes; the 2026 Standards independently support individualized DMMP-based school care and prescribed diabetes-technology use at school.
